questions.question: What is demographic parity?
choices: Different groups have equal true positive rates
Different groups receive positive predictions at the same rate
The overall model accuracy is above 90%
Each group has the same number of samples
questions.explanation: Demographic parity measures whether different groups receive positive predictions at similar rates. If Group A gets 40% positive predictions and Group B gets 15%, that's a demographic parity violation.

questions.question: Why is computing a single global fairness metric misleading?
choices: Averages mask disparities between different groups
Global metrics only work for binary classification
You need at least 10 groups for a global metric
questions.explanation: A system can have 85% overall accuracy but be 95% accurate for one group and 70% for another. Computing per-group metrics and comparing them reveals disparities that averages hide.

questions.question: How do you compute the demographic parity gap?
choices: Average the positive rates across all groups
Subtract the minimum positive rate from the maximum positive rate
Count how many groups have exactly the same rate
Divide the total positive predictions by total predictions
questions.explanation: The demographic parity gap is the difference between the highest and lowest positive prediction rates across groups. A gap of 0 means perfect parity; larger gaps indicate greater disparity.
